raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The denoise benchmark measured one request. `torch.compile` incurs its compile cost on the first request, so with `--torch-compile` the reported number was first-request latency, not steady state. The distortion scales inversely with step count (H100, 1024²):

| preset | single-shot | steady state | overstatement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| flux2-klein | 1.845 s | 0.275 s | 6.7x |
| zimage | 2.578 s | 0.623 s | 4.1x |
| ltx2 | 25.710 s | 7.408 s | 3.5x |

Eager pays no compile cost, so the error only inflates the compile arm — it skews compile-vs-eager comparisons, not just absolute numbers.

## Modifications

`--iterations` (default 4) runs N requests in one process and reports the fastest; request 1 loses the min by construction. Per-request timings come from stdout because the perf dump only ever holds request 1 (`cli/generate.py` writes `results[0]`), and the full series lands in `results_<label>.json`.

`SKILL.md` and `benchmark-and-profile.md`: document the default, and correct the Perf Dump Workflow — it directed readers to `compare_perf.py`, which reads the request-1 dumps, i.e. the cold numbers.

## Speed Tests

`flux2-klein`, 1×H100, 1024², `--torch-compile`, denoise seconds per request:

```
0.369  0.242  0.244  0.246   -> reported 0.242
```

Single-shot would have reported 0.369 s, 1.5x high. This run had a warm inductor cache; with a cold one the first request is several seconds and the gap is far larger.

## Checklist

- [x] pre-commit format
- [ ] unit tests
- [x] documentation
- [x] speed benchmark
- [x] code style

@@ -139,6 +139,17 @@ The helper defaults to eager. Add `--torch-compile` only for a labeled compile
 control. `--no-torch-compile` remains accepted for compatibility but is no

+The helper runs `--iterations` requests per measurement (default 4) in one
+process and reports the fastest. Request 1 pays `torch.compile` and first-shape
+specialization, so a single-shot number is first-request latency, not steady
+state -- on few-step models that overstates denoise latency several-fold, and
+only for the compile arm, which biases every compile-vs-eager ratio. The default
+is 4 because convergence is model-dependent: most presets settle after one
+request, `zimage-base` after three. Raise it when the per-request series in
+`results_<label>.json` is still sloping downward; a tail that never flattens is
+a recompilation bug rather than a warmup shortfall. Use `--iterations 1` only to
+reproduce a published single-shot number.
+
 The helper sets `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1` for accurate stage
 attribution. Set it to `0` explicitly only when collecting an e2e-only run and
 do not compare its per-stage values with synchronized results.

+differ several-fold. Take latency from `results_<label>.json`, which carries the
+reported minimum plus the per-request series; use the perf dump for stage
